summary.headline: Ganesha Ecosphere Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue up 41.2% YoY and 21.1% QoQ; consolidated EBITDA Rs 60.6 crore, Warangal RPSF fire weighed on margins.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 21.1% QoQ and 41.2% YoY, while standalone revenue rose 20.7% QoQ and 22% YoY, with consolidated sales volume at 49,382 tonnes versus 40,113 tonnes in Q1. Standalone EBITDA was Rs 24.51 crore and consolidated EBITDA Rs 60.6 crore, with consolidated EBITDA per tonne falling to Rs 14.92 from a Q1 level that included inventory gains. An August 2026 fire at the Warangal RPSF division halted that line, with fixed costs still incurred; the loss is said to be adequately covered by insurance and restoration is targeted by Q4 FY27. Management guided FY27 consolidated EBITDA to the higher end of the Rs 225–250 crore range, at roughly Rs 235–240 crore.

financial_highlights.change: Stated as up about 200% over the prior quarter
vs Q1 level that included inventory gains
Stated as up Rs 58.63 crore on prior-year half

segments.name: Standalone (PET/RPET, bottles-to-flakes and RPSF)
segments.commentary: Planned utilisation about 99% in Q2; sales volume 31,800 tonnes. Management says standalone margins hold at Rs 7–8/kg, and standalone EBITDA per tonne was Rs 70.04 per the transcript (the Rs 93.96 Q1 figure was stated alongside it). The RPSF line at Warangal is offline after the fire.

segments.name: Subsidiary Ganesha Ecopet (rPET granules / food-grade)
segments.commentary: Warangal utilisation about 67% in Q2; blended utilisation about 75% on lines operating through the quarter. Management guides subsidiary EBITDA of Rs 21–22/kg to hold, with Rs 22–24/kg blended after RPSF restoration, and a utilisation target of about 85% (90% by FY27 year-end per Q&A).

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated EBITDA guidance of Rs 225–250 crore; management expects the higher end, around Rs 235–240 crore.
Warangal RPSF line restoration expected by Q4 FY27; the OEM rejected the plant and imported equipment procurement is pending, so the line is targeted for end-February/March 2027.
Fifth rPET granule line under installation, commissioning expected in Q4 FY27; the fourth line has received FSSI food-grade approval.
Management expects no inventory gains in coming quarters, as inventory is turning fast and valued at current prices.
Subsidiary EBITDA expected at Rs 21–22/kg, with Rs 22–24/kg blended after RPSF restoration; standalone margin Rs 7–8/kg to be maintained.

Management indicated a further capacity plan (Odisha or northern India) with 50,000 tonnes costing about Rs 250–300 crore; the total targeted is about 1.5 lakh tonnes of rPET granules, with an announcement expected this quarter and commissioning 12–15 months after the decision.
capex_capacity: Warangal rPET granule capacity about 100,000 tonnes after line 5; no further expansion planned at Warangal.
Fifth rPET granule line at Warangal under installation, commissioning in Q4 FY27.
Kanpur RPSF production line being shifted to the Tamera unit to improve efficiency and integration.
New capacity of about 50,000 tonnes costs roughly Rs 250–300 crore and takes 12–15 months to commission; location is northern India or another site (Odisha was mentioned earlier in the call).
Warangal facility utilisation about 67% in Q2 FY27; the RPSF division was halted by the fire in August 2026 and insurance coverage is in place, with quantum of loss still under assessment.
demand_pricing: Management says the Indian FSSI-approved capacity is about 4.2–4.5 lakh tonnes, of which the company's approved capacity is now 65,000 tonnes; actual rPET sales in the market are about 25,000–30,000 tonnes a month, of which the company holds about 5,000 tonnes a month (about 20% share).
Around 85–90% of rPET capacity is on annual contracts with cost-plus, yield-linked pricing that passes raw material changes to buyers with about a one-month lag; the next renewal is in December.
Current prices: rPSF Rs 110–114/kg versus virgin PSF about Rs 150/kg; rPET about Rs 150/kg versus virgin PET Rs 140–145/kg.
Recycled polymer is priced at a discount to virgin polymer, supporting demand; the government mandate of 40% recycled content is in place and several new FSSI-approved capacities came online in Q2.
Management targets about 25% of India's rPET demand of about 1 million tonnes, and says the global brand owners make up 70–80% of its market and about 25 global brands are present in India.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current demand scenario for rPET, and have new FSSI-approved recyclers come online?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand is strong due to elevated virgin polymer prices and the 40% recycled-content mandate; new capacity came online in Q2 including a small northeast player and the company's own new line.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Warangal fire volume loss, and is inventory gain repeatable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the loss is roughly 2,500–3,000 tonnes; no inventory gains are expected going forward because inventory is valued at current prices and turns quickly.

qa_highlights.question: What are blended utilisation and EBITDA per kg trajectories for the subsidiary?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended utilisation about 75% in Q2; the new food-grade line ran at about 60% before FSSI approval and is ramping; target about 85%, with EBITDA Rs 21–22/kg maintained and Rs 22–24/kg blended after RPSF restoration.

qa_highlights.question: Is rPET Rs 21–22/kg EBITDA sustainable, and what is the contracted share?
qa_highlights.answer: 85–90% of capacity is on contract; management is confident of close to Rs 20/kg on a sustainable basis; 90% utilisation targeted by fiscal year-end through de-bottlenecking.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone volumes jump QoQ and what is the H2 run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Pent-up demand and inventory liquidation in Q2; management expects a run rate of about 28,000–29,000 tonnes per quarter, with the regular 29,000–30,000 level continuing into H2.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 EBITDA guidance of Rs 225–250 crore still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the higher end, about Rs 235–240 crore, driven by FSSI-approved mix in H2.

risks_watch: Crude and virgin polymer volatility affects both raw material and finished product prices; management says it cannot predict prices but current levels are elevated.
Warangal RPSF restoration depends on imported OEM equipment; a slip beyond Q4 FY27 would extend the loss of Rs i.e. the RPSF margin and fixed costs.
Contract renewal in December 2026 for the bulk of rPET volumes; competitors including Varun-type rivals signing their own brand partnerships could pressure renewal terms.
Promoter share pledge rising and cited as a 4% increase in the quarter, with repayment timing stated only as expected from the next quarter.
Export volumes have fallen due to freight costs and higher domestic prices; export outlook depends on Indian pricing.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and guidance, but cautious on price volatility: management repeatedly said prices are unpredictable and that the RPSF fire carries a double impact of lost margin plus fixed costs. Answers on the promoter pledge and the pending Odisha or northern India project were brief and less specific.
key_quotes: Demand fundamentals remain quite healthy. Our expansion projects are progressing as scheduled and we believe the momentum witnessed during the first half of the year should continue through the remainder of FI 27 as well.

So we are more than confident of getting the contracts number one number two, you know, even though a lot of players are there are coming are definitely yes, but the number one the quality of our pet output and as well as utilization.

adds.what: Fifth rPET granule line at Warangal (subsidiary Ganesha Ecopet)
New rPET granule capacity of about 50,000 tonnes (Odisha or northern India), announcement expected this quarter

growth.why: FY27 consolidated EBITDA guided to Rs 235–240 crore (upper end of Rs 225–250 crore), backed by 99% standalone utilisation, 85–90% of rPET capacity on annual cost-plus contracts, and a fifth Warangal line due Q4 FY27, though the RPSF line is offline after the August fire with restoration targeted by Q4 FY27 and the 50,000 t expansion is not yet approved.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Consolidated EBITDA per tonne fell to Rs 14.92 from a Q1 level that included inventory gains, with no inventory gains expected; subsidiary EBITDA guided at Rs 21-22/kg rising to Rs 22-24/kg blended only after RPSF restoration by Q4 FY27, and FY27 EBITDA guided at Rs 235-240 crore versus H1 Rs 120.42 crore.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Fifth rPET granule line at Warangal is under installation with commissioning in Q4 FY27, taking Warangal to about 100,000 t; the Warangal RPSF line is also targeted for reinstatement by Q4 FY27 after the August fire.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Standalone volume rose to 31,800 t from 25,321 t QoQ, management guides a run rate of 28,000-29,000 t per quarter, and the new fifth line adds capacity, although Warangal utilisation is only about 67% and the RPSF line is offline.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Standalone utilisation is about 99% and the Warangal line runs at 67%, and management expects an announcement this quarter for a 50,000 t capacity costing about Rs 250-300 crore (Rs 275 crore midpoint), with total target about 1.5 lakh t; the site is not yet approved.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management expects the higher end of the Rs 225-250 crore FY27 EBITDA range, about Rs 235-240 crore, driven by FSSI-approved mix in H2, but price volatility and the RPSF outage cap the upside.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: A slip in the imported OEM equipment for the Warangal RPSF line beyond Q4 FY27 would extend the lost margin and fixed costs, and the December 2026 renewal covers 85-90% of rPET capacity with pricing that could come under pressure.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: The fourth rPET granule line has received FSSI food-grade approval and the fifth line is due for commissioning in Q4 FY27, with the new food-grade line ramping from about 60% utilisation.

rows.label: Subsidiary utilisation ramp to 85-90%
rows.why: Blended utilisation is about 75% and management targets about 85%, with 90% by FY27 year-end through de-bottlenecking, while 85-90% of capacity is on annual contracts.

rows.label: Cost-plus contract renewal in December 2026
rows.why: Bulk of rPET volumes (85-90% of capacity) renews in December with cost-plus, yield-linked pricing that passes raw material changes with about a one-month lag, and rivals signing brand deals could pressure terms.

rows.label: Promoter share pledge rising
rows.why: Pledge rose about 4% in the quarter with repayment timing stated only as expected from the next quarter, and management gave brief, less specific answers on it.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, the FY27 EBITDA range and the fifth line, but cautious on crude-linked price volatility and the RPSF fire's double impact; analysts probed sustainability of the Rs 21-22/kg EBITDA, the inventory gain, and the promoter pledge, which got brief answers.
